extracted.intended_audience: general readers; students of literature, philosophy, and moral essays
extracted.subtask_description: Close reading of Montaigne's essay section arguing for the resemblance between human and animal faculties and critiquing human presumption. Focuses on examples and observations that indicate reason, communication, and social organization in animals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reason inferred from contrivance and tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Whatever we see in those bodies astonishes us: 'Quæ molitio, qua ferramenta, qui vectes, quæ machina, qui ministri tanti operis fuerunt?' — observe contrivance, tools, materials, engines employed in stupendous works as evidence of reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use visible complex structures and apparent design in animals and nature as grounds for attributing reasoning or intelligence rather than assuming mere brute instinct; question human exclusivity when faced with elaborate natural contrivances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejecting human presumption about superiority
rubrics_metrics.description: Presumption is our natural and original disease... in his imagination will be placing himself above the circle of the moon... The vanity of our presumption makes us prefer rather to owe our sufficiency to our own exertions than to her bounty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critically evaluate claims of human pre-eminence; treat assertions of human uniqueness as suspect vanity and test them against observation of other creatures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parity of faculties: communication between animals and humans
rubrics_metrics.description: They caress us, threaten us, and beg of us, and we do the same to them... we understand them no more than they do us; by the same reason they may think us to be beasts as we think them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess communicative behaviors (caressing, threatening, begging) as signs of shared social faculties; avoid assuming animals are merely mute or inaccessible to understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonverbal gestures constitute a public, intelligible language
rubrics_metrics.description: There is not a motion that does not speak... the alphabets upon the fingers, grammars in gesture, and the sciences which are only by them exercised and expressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count gestures, facial expressions, posture, and other nonverbal signs as meaningful, systematic modes of expression—parallel to spoken language and capable of conveying complex meanings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polity and division of labor as evidence of deliberation
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there a polity better ordered, the offices better distributed... than that of bees? Can we imagine such distribution of employments carried on without reasoning and deliberation?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use observed social organization (roles, division of labor, coordinated work) in animal communities as support for attributing collective deliberation or rule-governed behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliberate choice and foresight in nest-building and site selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The swallows... searching all the corners of our houses for the most commodious places wherein to build their nest... place their lodgings against the east, without knowing the different qualities of the winds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret selection of site, orientation, materials, and structural features in animal architecture as signs of discretion, foresight, and practical knowledge of environmental properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical knowledge in material use and construction
rubrics_metrics.description: In that elegant and admirable contexture of their buildings, can birds rather make choice of a square figure than a round... Do they bring water, and then clay, without knowing that the hardness of the latter grows softer by being wetted?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat purposeful use of materials (water+clay, moss for lining) and structural adjustments (tightening, knot types) as evidence of material understanding akin to technical reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution of complex, planned behavior (spider webs, knots, context-specific weaving)
rubrics_metrics.description: Why does the spider make her web tighter in one place, and slacker in another; why now make one sort of knot, and then another, if she has not deliberation, thought, and conclusion?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider context-dependent modifications in animal-made artifacts as indicative of problem-solving and adaptive planning rather than fixed automatism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-care and medicinal knowledge in animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Goats of Candia... choose out dittany for their cure; the tortoise... look for origanum to purge her; the dragon to rub and clear his eyes with fennel; the storks to give themselves clysters of sea-water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret selective ingestion or use of plants and substances for healing or cleansing as practical knowledge of remedies and causal relations in the environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem-solving and causal reasoning (raising liquid level)
rubrics_metrics.description: This dog... went and fetched stones and let them fall into the jar till he made the oil rise so high that he could reach it... ravens do the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat instances where animals use external objects to alter their environment (tool-like use) to achieve ends as strong evidence of causal reasoning and planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching, learning, and improvement through discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Aristotle... nightingales teach their young ones to sing... we may judge by this that they improve by discipline and study; the disciple listens to the master's lesson...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use intergenerational transmission, correction, practice, and emulation among animals as indicators of pedagogical structures and capacity for cultural learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity to sound and imitation as evidence of internal reason
rubrics_metrics.description: We teach blackbirds, ravens, pies, and parrots, to speak: the facility wherewith they lend us their voices... renders them so docile and willing to learn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count vocal imitation and the ability to map heard sounds onto produced sounds as signs of internal representation and cognitive flexibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical inference demonstrated in behavior (three-way path example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Chrysippus... considering the motions of a dog, who at three ways... 'he is not gone this way nor that, he must then infallibly be gone this other;' and assuring himself by this conclusion, he makes no use of his nose in the third way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret sequential elimination and inferential choice in animals as evidence of propositional reasoning analogous to human logical operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerical habits and sense of regularity (trained limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: The oxen... being ordered every one to draw a hundred turns a day, they were so accustomed to this number that it was impossible by any force to make them draw one turn more; but, their task being performed, they would suddenly stop and stand still.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider consistent, repeatable behavior tied to counts or quotas as signs of number-sense or habituated numerical competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation and fidelity in large-scale, risk-laden tasks (battle, hunting)
rubrics_metrics.description: They must necessarily have very confidently relied upon the fidelity and understanding of these beasts when they entrusted them with the vanguard of a battle... there are but few examples where it has happened that they have fallen foul upon their own troops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use coordinated behavior under danger (military, hunting) and reliable discrimination of allies/enemies as evidence of sophisticated social cognition and trustworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity for refined, learned performance under command (dancing, staged acting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Elephants taught to move and dance to the sound of the voice... a dog... served a player... counterfeit himself dead... then awaken at the proper time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge trained, timed, and multi-step performances as demonstrating memory, timing, inhibition, and responsiveness to abstract cues—cognitive abilities beyond reflex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observational humility: cultural bias in judging others as 'brutes'
rubrics_metrics.description: Who did not repute them savages and brutes!... All that seems strange to us, and that we do not understand, we condemn. The same thing happens also in the judgments we make of beasts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating unfamiliar peoples or creatures, account for cultural and perceptual bias; withhold moral or intellectual condemnation based solely on difference or lack of shared signs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature’s provisioning: equality in sufficiency of skins, senses, and faculties
rubrics_metrics.description: Our skins are as sufficient to defend us from the injuries of the weather as theirs are... There is in the polity of the world a greater equality and more uniform relation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess comparative claims about natural advantages by observing functional sufficiency rather than superficial differences; do not assume scarcity (e.g., lack of natural armor) implies inferiority.
